about: Published lap times of real GT3 cars at two of the five circuits we hold the geometry of, and the public GT3-class figures the Tornado GT3 was calibrated with on 2026-11-25. Facts (a time at a circuit, a power or weight figure), not a dataset: INDICATIVE, from news, results and manufacturer pages that are not the series' own timing, in qualifying trim. The test holds the car to them two ways: it must not lap faster than a real GT3 (0.95 x), and its quasi-steady lap at 100 % of its own limits must land within -3 % / +6 % of the real lap (the lap a driver at 92 % of the limits drives is not compared: that is driver margin, not the car). Retrieved 2026-11-24 / 2026-11-25.
licence: Facts (lap times) with their sources; no text reproduced.

laps.what: Sandy Mitchell, Lamborghini Huracan GT3 Evo, British GT qualifying: 2:16.984, reported as a British GT qualifying record
laps.confidence: low-medium: a single news report, national series, qualifying

laps.what: BMW M4 GT3 EVO, GT World Challenge Europe Sprint Cup qualifying: 1:23.617
laps.confidence: low-medium: a fan-run lap-record page citing the series, qualifying

not_found: No GT3 time was found for Monza, Silverstone or Suzuka (only GT4 and simulator times turned up); none is used.

figures_used.what: GT3 power is set by Balance of Performance, about 405-416 kW
figures_used.source: Porsche 911 GT3 R Evo up to 557 hp / 416 kW (ts2.tech comparison); Mercedes-AMG GT3 about 550 PS / 405 kW (Haupt Racing data page); both BoP-dependent
figures_used.confidence: low-medium: secondary sites, BoP changes per series and season

figures_used.source: Ferrari 296 GT3 1,250 kg (evo.co.uk, racingone.ps); Mercedes-AMG GT3 1,293 kg (lapmeta.com)

figures_used.what: Downforce about 870 kg at 250 km/h, i.e. a lift area of about 2.9 m2 (rho 1.225 kg/m3)
figures_used.used: downforce_area_m2 2.9 (was 1.48, i.e. about 440 kg at 250 km/h)
figures_used.source: Ferrari 296 Challenge 870 kg at 250 km/h (manufacturer figure on a dealer page, see data/physics/aero_reference.json race_car_downforce_evidence); floor: the road Porsche 992 GT3 RS makes 860 kg at 285 km/h (lift area about 2.2 m2). Unverified forum estimates of 860-920 kg at 241-250 km/h for other GT3 Evo cars were seen in a search result (page not opened) and are NOT used
figures_used.confidence: low: one manufacturer claim for a related car plus unverified forum estimates

figures_used.what: Drag area: a road 992 GT3 RS has Cd 0.39 with the wings flat (about 0.8 m2); a race GT3 with a full wing and widebody is higher
figures_used.used: drag_area_m2 1.17 (was 0.78): keeps lift/drag at 2.48, inside the checker's 2.5 envelope, with no extra unsourced claim
figures_used.source: Cd 0.39 with the wings flat for the 992 GT3 RS (excellence-mag.com 992 GT3 and GT3 RS Aero Tech); race value is our estimate

fitted_not_sourced: tyre peak friction scaled x1.26 (front lateral 1.52 -> 1.92, rear 1.56 -> 1.97; the largest factor that keeps every coefficient at or under the 2.0 cap of tools/physics/brake_reference.mjs): the one number fitted to the real laps; no published value exists
brake torque 7000 -> 9500 Nm: at 7000 Nm the brakes capped the stop at about 1.6 g whatever the tyres gave; now the tyres and ABS are the limit (1.68 g mean from 100 km/h)
brake bias 0.67 -> 0.72 (front share): at 1.9 g the ideal front share is 0.43 + 1.9 x h/L (0.156) = 0.73; at 0.67 the rear locked first and the test driver spun under braking at Silverstone
calibration.not_done_and_why: Only the GT3 has real lap references. The other 24 cars are de-branded originals with no named real counterpart in the catalogue, so there is no published figure to calibrate them against. Open: if a car should match a specific real car, name it and its published 0-100 / top speed / braking can be checked.
calibration.known_limit: The GT3's grip is understeer-limited at the steady-state limit (the front axle runs out first at about 1.6 g on the skidpad); a stiffer rear raises the car's limit to 1.66 g but the test driver cannot hold it. Chassis balance was not changed.
